trading.label: Trading
trading.note: Buy list — Stage 2 names near support.

stocks.name: Hindustan Copper Limited
stocks.fundamental: Government-owned Miniratna copper miner, holds all operating copper mining leases in India. Q1 FY27 revenue +81% to ₹937cr, PAT +162% to ₹352cr, EBITDA margin 54%. Two caveats worth weighing: sequentially profit actually fell 21% from Q4 FY26, so the YoY figure flatters; and auditors flagged governance gaps — no independent directors since Nov 2024 and no woman director since Mar 2025. Targets 4.7mt mine production in FY27. Reported talks with Codelco on Chilean supply are early-stage and unconfirmed.

stocks.name: Max Estates Ltd
stocks.fundamental: NCR real-estate developer (Noida and Gurugram), wellbeing-led LiveWell/WorkWell positioning. The headline is pre-sales: ~₹1,093cr in Q1 FY27, over 5x YoY, with 487 units sold against 43 a year ago, and ₹491cr collected. ICRA assigned a first-time A+ issuer rating. Commercial portfolio is 100% leased generating ₹150cr+ annual rent. But reported P&L is thin and going the other way — Q1 FY27 PAT fell 30% YoY to ₹8.35cr on revenue of ₹52cr, with EBITDA down 42%. That gap is normal for developers, where pre-sales convert to revenue only on construction milestones, but it means the accounts will lag the story for several quarters. GDV pipeline ₹16,150cr+.

momentum.label: Momentum
momentum.note: Strongest active trend right now. Aggressive — a Late-grade name here is a chase, not a buy.

stocks.name: Pakka Ltd
stocks.fundamental: Formerly Yash Pakka — compostable and moulded-fibre food packaging (Chuk brand), based in Ayodhya. Q1 FY27 rebounded in both revenue and profit after a sharp FY26 profit decline. Two real red flags: the auditor issued a qualified opinion over uncertainty on a major overseas project, and the board has approved USD 1mn to restart US operations. Small company — revenue in the ₹100-500cr band with roughly flat multi-year revenue CAGR and negative EBITDA CAGR. Treat the momentum as sentiment-driven; the accounts do not yet support it.

stocks.name: Khaitan Chemicals & Fertilizers Ltd
stocks.fundamental: Single super phosphate and sulphuric acid maker across MP, UP, Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh and Gujarat. Q1 FY27 PAT ₹10.9cr — up sharply sequentially but down 49% YoY from ₹21.4cr, on revenue of ₹221cr (−6% YoY). The segment split is the real story: fertilisers collapsed to ₹112cr from ₹187cr while chemicals grew to ₹110cr from ₹68cr. So the business is mid-rotation between segments rather than simply growing. Micro-cap, thinly traded.

stocks.name: Union Bank Of India Ltd
stocks.fundamental: PSU bank. Q1 FY27 standalone PAT +29.5% to ₹5,332cr, gross NPA down to 2.65% from 3.52% YoY, net NPA 0.47%, capital adequacy 18.46%, provision coverage ~95%. The catch is growth: deposit growth of ~3.5% badly trails the 8-9% guidance and credit growth of 12.5% is below target, so profit is coming from asset-quality improvement more than expansion.

stocks.name: PTC Industries Ltd
stocks.fundamental: PTC Industries — titanium and superalloy precision castings for aerospace and defence, via subsidiary Aerolloy. Q1 FY27 revenue +98% to ₹192cr and PAT +466% to ₹29cr, EBITDA margin expanding 954bps to 27.5%. Contracts with Airbus, BrahMos and the MoD point to a shift from component to systems supplier, and the UK subsidiary Trac Precision has stabilised. The catch is valuation: ~₹28,500cr market cap on ₹697cr trailing revenue and ₹126cr profit, trading at roughly 19x book, no dividend. Also note revenue and profit both fell sequentially from Q4 FY26.
